chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The elderly man and the one suffering from thirst, there is no blame upon them if they break their fast in the month of Ramadan, and each of them must give charity one mudd of food every day, and there is no make-up (qada) upon them; if they are unable [to give food], then there is nothing upon them.

key_terms.الْعُطَاشُ: One suffering from thirst or chronic illness
key_terms.مُدٍّ: A specific unit of volume for food

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for an elderly person who breaks their fast in Ramadan without making it up?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that chronic conditions like old age or persistent thirst exempt one from both making up fasts (qada) and paying the standard expiation (kaffarat al-fidya) if the food cannot be provided. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of progressive ease (taysir), where the obligation of feeding the poor is contingent upon actual financial and physical capacity, distinguishing it strictly from the temporary illness ruling.
